tables.name: Forest Encounters
entries: A tiny bearded man argues with a squawking raven. It holds something shiny in its beak.
A dryad sits atop a stone, a purple fungus lining her arms. There is violence in her eyes.
A patch of quicksand is disguised as soft ground. A broken spool of rope lies nearby.
A snarling pack of wolves surround a fresh kill. They are not keen to share.
Wild berries grow here in abundance. None have been eaten, not even by birds.
A trap, hastily set and poorly concealed. It smells strongly of urine.

tables.name: Unusual Weather
entries: An annual fog appears randomly, turning metallic surfaces to gold on contact.
An aurora that is visible even during the day.
Birds fly backwards, yet somehow still move forward.
Days are erratic. The Sun goes backwards for a time, then jumps forward as night rapidly sets in.
Distant chimes instead of thunder. A smoky, sweet wind blows in from the West.
Enormous, fleshy eyes peer down from the skies, their pupils lighting up the night sky.
Flashes of movement in the periphery that always amount to nothing.
Fog that fills the belly (no need for rations). Tomorrow, vomiting.
Lakes and streams evaporate in minutes, filling storm clouds that drench the landscape.
Periodic rains of small aquatic creatures (tadpoles, frogs, small fish). No one knows where they come from.
Rainbows lack most of their colors and occasionally flicker. Raindrops fall in various colors.
Rolling dust clouds that smell of cinnamon. The coughing lasts long after they've moved on.
Shadows disappear at random. Animals become more reluctant.
The air is thicker than usual, and breathing is difficult.
The clouds are shaped like faces. They appear to be laughing.
The moon appears larger and softly hums at night.
The rain glows gently at night. It can be gathered, but the light eventually fades.
The stars rearrange themselves in intricate patterns, making navigation difficult.
The winds carry whispers. Some say they tell hints of the future.
When it snows, the flakes are warm and dry.
